html:
The Rova of Antananarivo is the royal palace compound of the Merina kingdom, on the highest hill of Antananarivo in the highlands of Madagascar. It was founded in the early 17th century by King Andrianjaka.

Andrianjaka took the hill, fortified it and built the first royal house there. The town around it became the capital of Imerina. Later kings added wooden houses and royal tombs, and the hill became the sacred centre of the kingdom. Andrianampoinimerina and his son Radama I made Imerina the leading power of the island.

The tallest building, Manjakamiadana, was a great wooden palace built for Queen Ranavalona I around 1840. Under Ranavalona II, whose court turned Protestant, a British missionary architect wrapped it in stone. France ended the monarchy in 1897. In 1995 a fire gutted the compound; parts have since been rebuilt.
sum: The Rova of Antananarivo is the royal palace compound of the Merina kingdom, on the highest hill of Antananarivo in the highlands of Madagascar. It was founded in the early 17th century by King Andrianjaka.
